title: Arriving in Chicago and first jobs
summary: He sat in with Dixon, was hired by Cook and worked two jobs; he went to New York with Oliver in 1927.

story.theme_name: Chicago: the jazz migration and its clubs
story.community_name: Going north: working the Chicago jazz scene

blocks.x: Give them a job again. You went there in 25. What did you do when you got to Chicago? Had you ever played in Chicago before that? No.

Soon I arrived there. I went out. They arrived on a Sunday night. And I went to the entertainer and the Howard Dixon band was playing. I know they were playing trombone, huh? Yeah. And I walked in El Nong and I see the dude raised by them and said, I had a kid. And they had a break. They all came to the table and talked to me. I met Carl and all the boys and they insisted on me playing the numbers with them. And stuff with and asked me to play and I went to play. And Cook hired me to play. So I went out there and worked from 8 to 12. Next couple of days in order to do trade-taking, but I was so sick. Then I worked at two jobs.
Yeah, I worked first, you know, I went to go to work at 1 o'clock with Cal Dickerson. Oh, I see. Worked from 8 to 12 with Cook out at Lake. I started recording with Louie.
Then when I wound up I would record with 8 bands for 5 years. How long did you stay in Chicago? From 25 to 24 to 29.
Oh, that late. You were there all those years?
No, you went to New York. Oh, I went to New York, you know, with Oliver.
Came back. Oliver had no work and I came back and worked with Dave Payton.
